files.attribution: Earth textures: NASA Earth Observatory, Blue Marble Next Generation (Reto Stöckli, NASA GSFC), December 2004, topography and bathymetry, and Blue Marble topography (elevation). Public domain (NASA imagery is not copyrighted).
modifications: no free 3D model of the Earth's interior with separate layers was found (NASA 3D Resources, NIH 3D, Smithsonian 3D), so the layers are generated by the pipeline script
radii to scale for R = 2.4 units (6371 km): OuterCore 3480 km, InnerCore 1220 km; Crust exaggerated to 0.1 units (~265 km) so it is visible, Mantle just below it

flat section caps on every layer at the client's section plane (z = 0) with a procedural cross-section texture made by Bilig (rocky crust, mantle with schematic convection cells, liquid outer core with flow streaks, glowing inner core); the cores are emissive (KHR_materials_emissive_strength), the outer core glossy (KHR_materials_clearcoat)
crust: Blue Marble colour resized 5400×2700 → 2048×1024; relief normal map computed from the NASA elevation image (2048×1024, exaggerated); ocean gloss roughness map derived from both
atmosphere halo: three inward-facing translucent shells (AtmosphereHalo, extras.noPick)

Plate_Eurasian and Plate_Indian: schematic translucent patches with solid outlines over Central and South Asia, boundary along Makran – Himalaya – Burma arc, arrow for the Indian plate's northward motion (not survey data)
Quake_Kemin1911 (42.9° N 76.9° E) and Quake_Suusamyr1992 (42.1° N 73.6° E): approximate epicentre markers with a surface ring
globe turned so 75° E faces +Z (the camera); textures encoded WebP (EXT_texture_webp; KTX2 needs toktx, not available in the pipeline yet)
gltf-transform: dedup, prune, weld, EXT_meshopt_compression + quantisation
